newsitem.title: USA: California resolutions blast China on human rights.
newsitem.headline: California resolutions blast China on human rights.

text.p: A California state legislator has proposed resolutions calling on China to honour human rights in Hong Kong and condemning China's treatment of Christians and other religious groups, an aide said on Monday.

One of the resolutions introduced by Republican state Sen. Raymond Haynes called on China to preserve the political, civil and economic liberties of the people of Hong Kong and to retain democracy and free markets.

"The Chinese government deserves stern international condemnation for its atrocious abuses of fundamental human rights," Haynes said. "China cannot be allowed to export that human rights record to Hong Kong."

In another resolution Haynes accused China of religious persecution, claiming there were more documented cases of Christians being imprisoned or detained in China because of their religious beliefs than in any other country.

A California state senate committee was due to hear testimony on the Hong Kong resolution later on Monday. Chinese-American human rights activist Harry Wu, who spent 19 years in forced labour camps in China in the 1960s and 1970s, was scheduled to testify in its favour at the hearing.

Even though the resolutions would have no direct consequences if approved by the state legislature, a Haynes aide said the measures would send a message to Beijing and could prompt other states to take similar actions.
